security_frame.attacker: An attacker with authorized debug access, or physical access sufficient to enter scan mode, who wants to read a SHA-512 digest that the device computed before the transition into that state.
security_frame.precondition: The SHA-512 engine holds a digest in its SHA512_DIGEST register window. The device then transitions into debug-unlock or scan mode, which is precisely the transition the zeroize strobe exists to cover.
security_frame.input: No software input is required. The transition itself is the trigger: caliptra_top.sv:770 asserts debug_lock_or_scan_mode_switch on a debug-lock change, a scan-mode entry, a device-lifecycle change, or a fatal error.
security_frame.protected_asset: The SHA-512 digest result held in SHA512_DIGEST, which the hardware is supposed to wipe before a debug or scan path can observe it.
security_frame.modification: The DIGEST hardware-clear strobe was rewired through a second, inverted signal. sha512.sv:284-287 forms zeroize_reg2 = ~((~ZEROIZE) & debug_or_scan) alongside the correct zeroize_reg, and sha512.sv:300 drives the DIGEST hwclr from zeroize_reg2 while every other consumer in the same file, including the GEN_PCR_HASH_DIGEST hwclr on line 305, still uses zeroize_reg.

security_feature_bypassed: Hardware zeroization of the SHA-512 digest on debug-unlock or scan-mode entry. sha512_reg.rdl:83-85 states that ZEROIZE exists to 'Zeroize all internal registers after SHA process, to avoid SCA leakage', and the top level fans the same debug/scan switch out to nine crypto blocks as a shared secret-wipe convention.
proof_goal: Show that the rewired strobe inverts the digest clear with respect to the debug/scan input: the digest is NOT cleared when debug-unlock or scan-mode entry is signalled, and is instead held cleared while nothing is being requested. Show the software-ZEROIZE path still works, so the defect is a selective inversion rather than a wholesale break. Show the same testbench rejects the claim once the DIGEST hwclr is driven from the file's own surviving strobe (ZEROIZE || debug_or_scan), the one its other five zeroize consumers still use in a scratch copy.
minimum_attack_sequence: The SHA-512 engine computes a digest, which lands in the SHA512_DIGEST register window.
The device transitions into debug-unlock or scan mode. caliptra_top.sv:763-770 pulses debug_lock_or_scan_mode_switch on that transition and fans it to every crypto block.
Under the convention the rest of the tree follows, zeroize_reg = ZEROIZE | debug_or_scan goes high and the DIGEST window is wiped before the debug or scan path can observe it.
In this tree the DIGEST hwclr is driven by zeroize_reg2 = ~((~ZEROIZE) & debug_or_scan) instead, which evaluates to 0 in exactly that case, so no clear occurs.
The digest remains in the register window and is observable through the debug or scan path that the transition just opened.
expected_evidence: sha512.sv:284-287 forms two strobes where every other block in the tree forms one, and the second is ~((~ZEROIZE) & debug_or_scan).

sha512.sv:300 drives the DIGEST hwclr from zeroize_reg2; sha512.sv:305 drives the neighbouring GEN_PCR_HASH_DIGEST hwclr from zeroize_reg, so the inconsistency is local rather than a deliberate redefinition.
The DIGEST write-enable suppression on line 298, the BLOCK hwclr on line 314, the internal register-clear branch at line 229, and all four submodule .zeroize ports still use the original zeroize_reg.

Computed census: the audited tree's own census of zeroize-driven hwclr sites: 22 sites across 6 crypto blocks (doe, ecc, hmac, sha256, sha512, soc_ifc), 20 driven from the correct strobe and exactly 2 driven from an inverted one, sha512.sv:300 and sha256.sv:403, both of them DIGEST windows. The design's own convention therefore convicts the outlier, and the same file drives its five other zeroize consumers from the correct strobe.

Exactly two files in the whole audited tree contain a zeroize_reg2, sha512.sv and sha256.sv, and they are precisely the two inverted sites, so the construct is a local deviation rather than a tree-wide idiom.
sha512_reg.rdl:83-85 states the security purpose of ZEROIZE and marks it singlepulse.
sha512_reg.sv:905-922 shows the DIGEST hwclr reaching a branch that drives the field to zero, so the strobe is live.
caliptra_top.sv:770 shows the switch asserted on debug-lock change, scan-mode entry, lifecycle change, or fatal error, and is fanned out to nine blocks.

In simulation with debug_or_scan asserted, a value seeded into the DIGEST window survives; with the DIGEST hwclr driven from the file's own surviving strobe (ZEROIZE || debug_or_scan), the one its other five zeroize consumers still use in a scratch copy, the identical testbench finds it wiped.
In simulation the software-ZEROIZE path still clears the window on this RTL, confirming the inversion is selective.
success_criteria: Every structural gate holds, including the computed census that measures the tree's own convention and the in-file controls that show every other consumer of the strobe was left alone.
The directed simulation observes the digest surviving debug/scan assertion, with a nonzero cover count so the result cannot be vacuous, and with a control check proving the probe itself works.
The negative control fails on patched RTL while its software-ZEROIZE control check still passes, establishing that the testbench discriminates rather than always passing.
The behaviour is reported from simulation rather than asserted from the expression by inspection. The testbench drives both values of debug_or_scan and prints what the hardware does in each case.

The quiescent-case side effect (the window held cleared when nothing is requested) is reported but not asserted as the security claim, since it is a functional consequence of the same inversion rather than an independent finding.

The companion sha256.sv site is recorded so the mitigation covers both blocks. No separate impact claim is made for it here; the SHA-256 DIGEST window is declared sw = r (sha256_reg.rdl:132), so it was not used as the probe.
No claim is made that this bug alone yields a private key. The asset exposed is a SHA-512 digest result; what that discloses depends on what was hashed.
